svg.title: Thesis pipeline flow v2 — upstream data prep, Part 1 rule discovery, Part 2 predictive evaluation
svg.desc: Three-stage pipeline: scripts 1-2 produce continuous and discretized datasets; Part 1 detrends the target then mines rules with three algorithms; Part 2 runs walk-forward evaluation comparing five models including two CarenR variants.
svg.text: Thesis Pipeline — v2: Upstream Data Prep · Part 1 Rule Discovery · Part 2 Predictive Capacity
RDD (Douro, ~89 obs) · RVV (Vinho Verde, ~80 obs) · linear detrending applied to TARGET only
STAGE 0 · DATA PREPARATION · upstream of run_all_pipelines.R
Feature discretization happens HERE. After this stage two parallel files exist on disk per region.
alignment by year, base feature set
(target Wine_mhl stays numeric in BOTH outputs)
Important: discretization in Stage 0 is applied ONLY to features. Wine_mhl is left numeric in both files; what happens to the target depends on the algorithm in Part 1 / Part 2.
Per region, full dataset. Each algorithm gets its own target transformation; features are NOT touched.
IF cond THEN Wine_mhl = a₀ + Σaᵢxᵢ
Part 1 deliverable — qualitative comparison of rule LANGUAGES
distributional vs. classification vs. piecewise-linear, on the same regions
Walk-forward, expanding window. min_train = 25, step_years = 1. All models trained fresh per scenario.
train = years[1..te] · test = years[te+1..n] · linear trend FIT ON TRAIN ONLY (fold-correct), residuals fed to models
Data routing in Part 2: Naive · DT · M5Rules read the CONTINUOUS dataset. CarenR_Assoc reads the DISCRETIZED dataset (mining and prediction).
CarenR_Dist mines on DISCRETIZED data, but the parsed interval rules are applied to CONTINUOUS test rows so they fire on raw feature values.
Predictions reverted to mhl (+ trend offset) → MAE · RMSE · R²
computed against actual Wine_mhl on the test split
Part 2 deliverable — head-to-head: Naive vs DT vs CarenR_Assoc vs CarenR_Dist vs M5Rules
across both RDD and RVV, over the full sweep of training sizes
Order of operations: Stage 0 discretizes FEATURES (target stays numeric). Part 1 / Part 2 detrend the TARGET. RIPPER additionally bins the residual target into Low/Med/High AFTER detrending.
Detrending in Part 1 uses the full dataset; detrending in Part 2 is fold-correct (trend fitted on training only, applied to test).
Predictions in Part 2 always converted back to mhl (residual + trend offset) before scoring against actual Wine_mhl.
